authoredPrompt: This figure is part of a worked example asking to use Pappus' Theorem to find the volume of the torus generated by revolving a circular region of radius b about an axis at distance a from the center of the circle. The figure shows a 3D torus in perspective with the vertical axis of revolution passing through its central hole; the distance a from the axis to the center of the circular cross-section and the radius b of the cross-section are labeled, with the cross-section highlighted as a small circle on the right side of the torus. A red dashed ellipse traces the circular path traveled by the centroid, with direction arrows, and a caption box reads The centroid travels a distance 2pi a. The figure shows that by Pappus' Theorem the volume V = (2 pi a)(pi b^2) = 2 pi^2 a b^2, since the centroid traverses a full circle of circumference 2 pi a as the region revolves.
authoredInteractions:
- Sliders for major radius a and tube radius b: reshape the torus in real time and display the updated volume (2π²ab²) and surface area (4π²ab) via Pappus's theorem
- Animate the generating circle of radius b revolving around the axis to show how the torus is formed and trace the red centroid path of length 2πa
- Drag to rotate the 3D torus to inspect its shape from any viewpoint
authoredContext:
Use Pappus’ Theorem to find the volume V of the torus generated by revolving a circular region of radius b about a line at a distance a (greater than b) from the center of the circle (Figure 5.7.13). By symmetry, the centroid of a circular region is its center. Thus, the distance
traveled by the centroid is 2πa. Since the area of a circle of radius b is πb2, it follows from
Pappus’ Theorem that the volume of the torus is
V = (2πa)(πb2
) = 2π2
ab2

discrepancies: The blue cross-section circle and yellow fill are built in the YZ plane (points (a, b·cosθ, b·sinθ)) instead of the meridional plane containing the axis, so the slice does not lie on the torus surface and reads as a faint edge-on ellipse rather than the bold full circle facing the viewer in the source.

The red dashed centroid path and its two direction arrowheads are washed out to pale pink because they sit inside the semi-transparent torus and are occluded, whereas in the source the dashed loop and arrowheads are crisp and clearly on top.
The 'a', 'b', and 'The centroid travels a distance 2πa' labels are far too small to read comfortably, losing the clear hierarchy of the source.
The large tan callout arrow that points from the caption box up to the dashed path in the source is absent; only a tiny caption chip remains.
The camera is more top-down than the source's front-elevated 3/4 view, which hides the torus hole's depth and makes the right-side cross-section appear edge-on.
evaluation.notes: The torus, vertical axis, center dot, dimension lines, and Pappus formulas are correct and the sliders/animate button are genuinely pedagogical, but the cross-section slice is oriented in the wrong plane, the red centroid path is occluded and faint, the prominent callout arrow is missing, and all text labels are too small.
action_items: Rebuild the cross-section circle and fill in the meridional plane (parameterize as (a + b·cosθ, b·sinθ, 0) at the chosen radial angle) so the slice lies on the torus surface and appears as a full circle facing the camera.
Make the red dashed centroid path and its arrowheads clearly visible (e.g. set depthTest false / renderOrder high, or lower torus opacity) so they match the bold dashed loop in the source.
Increase the font sizes of the 'a', 'b', and caption labels and add the large tan callout arrow from the caption to the path.
Adjust the initial camera to a more front-elevated 3/4 view (lower azimuth, moderate elevation) so the torus hole and the right-side cross-section read like the source.
